tei:titleStmt.tei:title: מימיני מיכאל
"Mikhael is on my right," an apotropaic invocation of angelic protection in the Bedtime Shema from the Maḥzor Vitry (ca. 11th c.)

tei:div.tei:head: "Mikhael is on my right," an apotropaic invocation of angelic protection in the Bedtime Shema from the Maḥzor Vitry (ca. 11th c.)

tei:lg.tei:l: May Mikhael be on my right,

tei:note.tei:p: Sanoi [Sana’ui according to Moses Zacutto]), derived from the initials of three words samim nataf ush’chelet — “sweet spices, stacte, and onycha,” in Exodus 30:34. Thanks to Jacobus Swart for his explanation.
Sansanoi [Sansina’ui according to Moses Zacutto]), is a variant of the word b’sansinav — “of the boughs thereof” in Song of Songs 7:9. Thanks to Jacobus Swart for his explanation.

A variant spelling for the angel Semangelof. The name appears as סנמגליי in the British Library MS. 27200 v.23r. In JTSA MS. 8092, the –וף ending of סמנגלוף follows on the next line. Abraham Berliner transcribed it as סנמגלי. Semanglof is said to have originated from the words samim ul’vonah zakah — “sweet spices with pure frankincense”, also found in Exodus 30:34 (see above note on ‘Sanoi’). Thanks to Jacobus Swart for his explanation.
